mergedParams.userDescription: A single word moving in a slow, precise arc across the scene. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Slow Arc Typography - Single Word Motion

prompts.prompt: Create a 'typokinetics' preset that animates a single word along a smooth, cinematic arc path - like a title card gracefully entering and exiting frame in a high-end motion graphics piece. The word should follow a bezier curve trajectory, starting from below the visible area on the left, rising to peak at the center-top of the screen, then descending off-screen to the right. Think of how a movie title might arc across the screen in a dramatic opening sequence. The animation should feel weighted and deliberate, with the word subtly rotating to follow the tangent of the arc path, creating a sense of the text 'riding' the curve. Add a subtle motion blur effect during the fastest parts of the movement and a gentle fade-in/out at the trajectory endpoints. The word should maintain perfect readability throughout the arc, with optional letter-spacing expansion at the apex for dramatic emphasis.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use a BaseLayout container with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' classes. Create a TextAtom for the word with absolute positioning. Implement the arc motion using a generic keyframe effect with translateX and translateY properties that follow cubic bezier control points (start: translateX: -50%, translateY: 100% → mid: translateX: 0%, translateY: -20% → end: translateX: 50%, translateY: 100%). Add rotation effect synced to the arc tangent (rotate: -15deg → 0deg → 15deg). Apply opacity effect (0 → 1 → 0) with 20% fade-in/out at trajectory ends. Use 'ease-in-out' easing with a 4-6 second duration. Add blur effect (2px → 0px → 2px) at movement peaks. For the TextAtom, use 'text-6xl font-bold tracking-normal' classes, with a letterSpacing effect that expands from 0 to 0.2em at the arc apex. Consider using fitDurationTo: 'self' to ensure the animation completes within the preset duration. Performance: use transform-gpu and will-change-transform classes.

prompts.prompt: Design a 'typokinetics' preset inspired by minimalist Swiss typography, where a single word glides horizontally across the scene in a perfectly straight line with mathematical precision. The word should move at a constant, slow velocity - like reading a single line of text in extreme slow motion. As it travels, implement a subtle 'depth of field' effect where the word gradually comes into sharp focus at the center of the screen, then softly blurs again as it exits. Think of it as a typographic version of a focus pull in cinematography. The word should have a clean, sans-serif appearance with generous letter-spacing that contracts slightly as it reaches the focal point, creating a subtle breathing effect. Add a very faint drop shadow that shifts angle based on the word's position, suggesting a fixed light source.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'flex items-center justify-center w-full h-full' classes. Position TextAtom with 'absolute top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2' for vertical centering. Create a linear horizontal movement using translateX effect from -120% to 120% with 'linear' easing over 8-10 seconds. Implement focus effect using blur filter (3px → 0px → 3px) with peak sharpness at screen center (50% of animation). Apply letterSpacing effect (0.3em → 0.1em → 0.3em) synchronized with focus. For the drop shadow, use textShadow effect that interpolates the offset angle: start: '2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.2)' → center: '0px 4px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)' → end: '-2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.2)'. Use TextAtom with 'text-5xl font-light uppercase' classes. Set font to 'Inter:300:normal' or similar clean typeface. Consider adding a subtle opacity ramp (0.7 → 1 → 0.7) for entry/exit. Performance: utilize transform3d for GPU acceleration.

prompts.prompt: Build a 'typokinetics' preset that treats the word like a pendulum swinging through space - perfect for dramatic title reveals or impactful caption moments. The word should swing in from the top-left corner as if suspended by an invisible string, reaching its lowest point at center-bottom, then continuing its arc up to the top-right before swinging back slightly in a dampened oscillation. Think of Newton's cradle or a hypnotic pendulum motion. The word should rotate naturally with the swing, tilting left and right to maintain the illusion of weight and momentum. Add a dynamic scaling effect where the word grows larger as it approaches the viewer (bottom of swing) and shrinks with distance. Include a subtle motion trail or echo effect during the fastest parts of the swing to emphasize the kinetic energy.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full' classes. Use TextAtom with transform-origin set to 'top center' via style prop. Implement pendulum motion with chained keyframe effects: Primary swing uses translateX (-40% → 0% → 40% → -10% → 0%) and translateY (-60% → 20% → -60% → 10% → 0%) with custom cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) easing over 5 seconds. Rotation effect syncs with swing: rotate (-25deg → 0deg → 25deg → -5deg → 0deg). Scale effect for depth: scale (0.8 → 1.2 → 0.8 → 1.0 → 1.0). For motion trail, create 2-3 duplicate TextAtoms with decreasing opacity (0.3, 0.15, 0.05) and slight animation delay offsets (0.05s, 0.1s, 0.15s). Each trail element uses 'absolute pointer-events-none' classes. Main TextAtom uses 'text-7xl font-bold' classes. Consider adding a subtle perspective transform to the container for enhanced 3D effect. Use fitDurationTo: 'self' and adjust playback rate if needed.

prompts.prompt: Develop a 'typokinetics' preset where the word moves in a spiral pattern, starting from the outer edge and spiraling inward to the center, then holding briefly before fading out - like water going down a drain or a hypnotic spiral animation. The word should decrease in size as it spirals inward, creating a vortex effect. As it moves, apply a rotational motion that increases in speed as the word approaches the center, simulating angular momentum conservation. Think of it as typography caught in a whirlpool. Add a subtle color shift or hue rotation as the word spirals, transitioning from cool to warm tones. The word should also gradually increase in blur as if moving faster, then snap into perfect focus when it reaches the center point.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center' classes. Position TextAtom absolutely with initial placement at edge. Implement spiral using parametric equations in keyframe effects: For 3 complete rotations, create 24 keyframes where translateX = radius * cos(angle) and translateY = radius * sin(angle), with radius decreasing from 45% to 0% and angle increasing from 0 to 1080deg. Apply simultaneous rotate effect (0deg → 1080deg) for spinning motion. Scale effect decreases from 1.5 to 0.6 as word spirals inward. Implement acceleration using non-linear easing - start with ease-out, transition to ease-in for final approach. Color effect using filter: hue-rotate(0deg → 180deg). Blur effect: blur(0px → 3px → 0px) with sharp focus at center. Final hold at center for 1 second with opacity fade (1 → 0) over last 0.5s. TextAtom uses 'text-5xl font-semibold' classes. Total duration: 6-7 seconds. Consider using internal effect preset for the spiral motion for reusability.

prompts.prompt: Create a 'typokinetics' preset inspired by typewriter mechanics, where the word slides in character by character from the right edge, but instead of appearing instantly, each letter follows its own subtle arc trajectory - like typewriter keys striking paper. The complete word should assemble at the center, hover briefly with a subtle vibration effect (mimicking the impact), then continue sliding off to the left as a complete unit. Think of mechanical precision meets organic motion. Each letter should have a slightly different arc height and timing offset, creating a cascading wave effect. Add a subtle 'ink spread' effect using a brief scale pulse when each letter lands. The assembled word should have a moment of perfect stillness before the exit motion begins.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' classes. If caption data is available, split word into individual TextAtoms for each letter; otherwise, use CSS letter-spacing animation. For multi-letter approach: Create array of TextAtoms, each with staggered start times (0.1s offset per letter). Each letter follows arc trajectory: translateX (100% → final position) and translateY (0% → -20% → 0%) with bounce easing. Individual letter scale pulse on landing: scale(1 → 1.15 → 1) over 0.2s. After assembly (1.5s), apply vibration using rapid translateX/Y oscillations (±2px) for 0.3s. Exit motion: entire word group translates left (-120%) with ease-in over 1.5s. Use 'inline-block' for each letter TextAtom with 'text-5xl font-mono' classes. Container uses 'flex items-center justify-center' with absolute positioned letter containers. Consider using repeatChildrenProps for letter styling consistency. Add subtle textShadow on impact for depth.

prompts.prompt: Design a 'typokinetics' preset where the word follows a figure-eight (infinity symbol) path, creating a mesmerizing continuous motion perfect for background titles or ambient typography. The word should complete one full figure-eight loop, with the crossing point at the screen center. As it moves, implement a 'twist' effect where the word appears to rotate in 3D space, showing different perspectives as it navigates the curves. Think of it as typography on a möbius strip. The word should scale up slightly when passing through the center crossing point, as if coming closer to the viewer. Add a subtle trail effect that fades quickly, creating a sense of fluid motion. Include a gentle pulsing glow that intensifies at the curve peaks.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full' classes as container. TextAtom positioned absolutely at path start. Implement figure-eight using Lissajous curve equations in effects: translateX follows sin(t) * 40% and translateY follows sin(2t) * 25% where t progresses from 0 to 2π over animation duration. Add perspective rotation using rotateY effect (-30deg → 30deg → -30deg) synchronized with horizontal position. Scale effect at center crossing: scale(1 → 1.2 → 1) with 0.3s duration at midpoint. For trail effect, create 3 duplicate TextAtoms with opacity 0.4, 0.2, 0.1 and animation delays of 0.1s, 0.2s, 0.3s respectively. Glow effect using textShadow: alternate between '0 0 10px rgba(255,255,255,0.3)' and '0 0 20px rgba(255,255,255,0.6)' at curve peaks. TextAtom uses 'text-6xl font-bold' classes. Duration: 8-10 seconds for smooth motion. Use 'ease-in-out' for natural acceleration through curves. Consider transform-style: preserve-3d for true 3D rotation.

prompts.prompt: Build a 'typokinetics' preset with physics-based motion, where the word 'bounces' across the screen like a rubber ball. The word enters from top-left with diagonal momentum, bounces off the bottom edge with realistic deformation and energy loss, continues to bounce with decreasing height until it settles and rolls off-screen. Each bounce should include a squash-and-stretch effect on the word itself. Think of classic animation principles applied to typography. The word should rotate based on its 'rolling' motion between bounces. Add a subtle shadow that grows/shrinks based on the word's height from the 'ground'. Include a slight wobble effect after each impact to simulate elasticity.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full' classes, representing the 'floor' at bottom. TextAtom starts at top-left with initial velocity. Implement gravity-based motion using multiple keyframe segments: First drop: translateY (-80% → 60%) with ease-in (acceleration), translateX (-40% → -20%). First bounce: translateY (60% → 20%) with ease-out (deceleration), scaleY (1 → 0.7 → 1.2 → 1) for squash-stretch, rotate (0deg → 180deg). Subsequent bounces with 0.7x height reduction each time. Between bounces, add rolling rotation proportional to horizontal travel. Shadow effect using box-shadow that scales with height: '0 Ypx 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.3)' where Y = word height * 0.5. Wobble effect post-bounce: rapid scaleX oscillations (1 → 1.05 → 0.95 → 1) over 0.2s. TextAtom uses 'text-5xl font-bold' classes with 'inline-block' for transform origin accuracy. Total duration: 5-6 seconds. Consider using spring easing for bounce segments. Final roll-off uses linear translateX to 120%.

prompts.prompt: Create a 'typokinetics' preset inspired by cinematic depth-of-field rack focus, where the word moves through Z-space (toward/away from viewer) while traveling horizontally. The word starts small and blurred in the background, moves forward and across the screen coming into sharp focus at the center, then continues moving toward the viewer becoming large and blurred again as it passes 'through the camera'. Think of a dolly zoom combined with lateral movement. The word should have perspective distortion at extreme positions. Add a subtle chromatic aberration effect at the blur extremes to simulate lens optics. Include a slight rotation that follows the perspective shift, as if the word is mounted on a track.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full perspective-1000 overflow-hidden' classes for 3D space. TextAtom positioned with transform3d. Implement Z-axis movement using scale (0.3 → 1 → 2.5) to simulate depth, combined with translateX (-60% → 0% → 60%) for horizontal movement and translateZ for true 3D if supported. Blur effect matches Z-position: blur(8px → 0px → 12px). Chromatic aberration using CSS filters at extremes: apply split color channels with slight offset via filter or text-shadow RGB separation. Perspective rotation: rotateY (20deg → 0deg → -20deg) following camera angle. Add subtle rotateZ (-5deg → 0deg → 5deg) for track movement. TextAtom uses 'text-6xl font-bold' with initial 'opacity-0' transitioning to visible. Duration: 6-7 seconds with ease-in-out. Consider using will-change: transform, filter for performance. At peak focus (center), hold for 0.5s for readability. Use transform-style: preserve-3d on container.

prompts.prompt: Develop a 'typokinetics' preset where the word follows a smooth wave pattern across the screen, undulating up and down like text floating on ocean waves. The word should maintain its horizontal orientation while riding the wave peaks and troughs. As it moves, implement a subtle 'liquid' distortion effect where the word appears to bend and flex with the wave motion. Think of typography made of flexible material responding to wave forces. The word should also gently rotate forward and backward as it climbs and descends the waves. Add a shimmering effect at wave peaks where the word catches the light. Include subtle letter-spacing changes that expand in troughs and contract at peaks, as if affected by wave compression.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' classes. TextAtom follows sine wave path using compound effects: translateX (-100% → 100%) with linear progression, translateY follows sin(4πt) * 15% for 2 complete waves across screen width. Rotation effect: rotateZ oscillates between -10deg and 10deg following wave derivative (steeper climb = more tilt). For liquid distortion, apply skewY effect (-5deg → 5deg) alternating with wave phase. Letter-spacing effect: varies from 0.05em to 0.15em inversely with wave height. Shimmer effect at peaks using brightness filter (100% → 130% → 100%) and subtle textShadow glow. TextAtom uses 'text-5xl font-medium' classes. Duration: 7-8 seconds for smooth wave riding. Consider adding subtle scaleY (0.95 → 1.05) for vertical stretch/compression. Use cubic-bezier easing for more organic wave motion. Optional: add very subtle hue-rotate filter for color shimmer.

prompts.prompt: Build a 'typokinetics' preset with a magnetic attraction effect, where the word starts at a random edge position and gets pulled toward the center through an invisible magnetic field. The word should accelerate as it gets closer to the center (following inverse square law), overshoot slightly, then oscillate back and forth with dampening until it settles at the center point. Think of it as typography affected by gravitational pull. As the word accelerates, add increasing motion blur and a slight size increase to emphasize the speed and proximity. The word should also rotate slowly throughout the motion, as if tumbling through space. Include an electric/energy glow effect that intensifies as the word approaches the center, suggesting the magnetic field strength.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center' classes. TextAtom starts at random edge (use Math.random() in preset logic or fixed position). Implement acceleration using custom easing - create multi-segment animation: Initial slow drift (ease-in), rapid acceleration (exponential ease), overshoot with spring physics. Position animation: translateX and translateY from start to 0 with 5-7 keyframes showing acceleration curve. Overshoot by 10% past center, then oscillate with decreasing amplitude (10% → -5% → 2% → 0). Rotate effect: continuous slow rotation (0deg → 720deg) over full duration. Scale effect: grows from 1 to 1.3 as approaching center, settles at 1.1. Blur effect: increases with velocity (0px → 4px → 0px). Glow using textShadow: intensifies from '0 0 5px rgba(100,200,255,0.2)' to '0 0 30px rgba(100,200,255,0.8)' at center. TextAtom uses 'text-6xl font-bold' classes. Total duration: 4-5 seconds. Use will-change: transform for smooth animation.
